rationale: B is better structured, more actionable, and materially more accurate about PACS integration: it uses standard ORU^R01 result messaging, separates event triggering, DICOMweb retrieval, inference, and worklist integration, and gives more realistic study-level latency and external-validation guidance. A contains serious implementation errors, notably nonexistent or misused HL7 message types such as ORU^OBS and ORU^RSL, an implausible sub-two-second whole-study CT target, and overly prescriptive training advice such as freezing the backbone after two epochs. B still overstates several points—including universal ViT superiority, DICOMweb subscriptions as a general facility, mandatory TLS 1.3, and the ease of deploying uncleared software as CDS—but its overall architecture and reasoning provide the stronger engineering plan.
